questions.question: When you see a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended, you should:

options.text: Stop completely and wait before moving forward.
Honk your horn and pass the bus on the left.
Keep driving when you think the children have finished getting off.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait before moving forward.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when you see a school bus with its stop arm out. Do not move forward until the stop arm is pulled back in.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol harms your vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

questions.question: Before driving while taking over-the-counter medicine, you should:

options.text: Read the label on the medicine.
Drive no matter what the warning label says.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the label on the medicine.
questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving. Always read the label for warnings. If you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist whether you can safely drive while taking the medicine.

questions.question: When an aggressive driver is near you, you should:

options.text: Do not look at them, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Show them you disapprove of their driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not look at them, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and create distance between you and the aggressive driver. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make gestures at them.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of you. You should:

options.text: Speed up and drive past the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to stop when you see pedestrians near or crossing the road. Be extra careful around children. Always let pedestrians cross in crosswalks.

questions.question: To change lanes safely, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal first, check your mirrors, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal first, check your mirrors, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal and check both mirrors. Then look over your shoulder to see your blind spot. Make sure no other car is moving into the same lane. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: Which statement about seat belts and child safety seats is true?

options.text: Never put a baby in the front seat of a car with airbags.
An airbag can hurt a baby or small child, even in a small crash.
All passengers must wear a seat belt or use a child safety seat.

questions.explanation: Always wear your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child safety seats. Seat belts greatly reduce your chance of injury or death in a crash. Children 12 and under must sit in the back seat, properly restrained. Never place a rear-facing infant seat in the front of a car with a front airbag.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:
questions.explanation: Brake lights show other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping. Always keep your brake lights working when you drive.

questions.question: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and let them have the right-of-way. Drive carefully and be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you there is a traffic light coming up. Be ready to stop for a red light or slow down for a yellow light. Watch for cross traffic.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn into an exit. If you miss your exit, drive to the next one instead.

questions.question: Who must wear a seat belt?
questions.explanation: North Dakota law requires all drivers and front seat passengers to wear seat belts. Children under 18 must be properly secured in seat belts or child restraint systems, no matter where they sit in the vehicle.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Look in your rearview and side mirrors to check if anyone is passing you. Also look over your shoulder to see if anyone is in your blind spot.

questions.question: What should you do if you miss your exit on an interstate expressway?

options.text: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Drive to the next exit and safely turn around there.

questions.question: When is it important to slow down?

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, at intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp or blind curves, where there are pedestrians or hazards, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: How can you help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
questions.explanation: To help prevent road rage, use proper turn signals, obey posted speed limits, and allow plenty of extra time for your trip.

questions.question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Try to get out of the aggressive driver's way.
Stare at the driver as he or she is passing you.
Speed up as he or she is passing you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to get out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver is behind you, get out of their way. Avoid making eye contact. Do not speed up or challenge them, as this may make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: Why shouldn't you follow other cars too closely?

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the vehicle in front of you slows or stops suddenly.
You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.
You may not see the other vehicle's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the vehicle in front of you slows or stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely, you won't have enough time to stop if the car in front of you suddenly slows down or stops. This can cause a collision.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in a school zone unless otherwise posted?
questions.explanation: The speed limit in a school zone is 20 miles per hour unless a different speed is posted. Always drive carefully in school zones.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Highway changes ahead and to the right.
Hiking trails ahead and to the right.
Hotel ahead and to the right.
Hospital ahead and to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hospital ahead and to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a hospital with emergency services is located to the right.

questions.question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder every time you move your vehicle. This includes turning, changing lanes, and pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?

options.text: When a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop your vehicle at stop signs, at red lights, and whenever a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep downhill grade is coming.

questions.question: How should you drive safely at night?

options.text: Do not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.

questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see. Follow these steps to keep yourself and other drivers safe.

questions.question: If a traffic officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Do what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.explanation: Traffic signals help keep traffic moving safely. Drivers must obey traffic lights, but when a traffic officer is directing traffic, you must follow the officer's directions instead.
